D: A divorced dad disguises himself as an elderly British nanny to spend time with his kids.
P: Serve dessert when Daniel's face ends up in the frosting.
S: the dinner where he runs between two tables all night

Green prawns tossed fast in foaming garlic and chilli butter with lemon and parsley, crusty bread to mop it up. Go easy on the cayenne. Melt 80g butter in a large pan until foaming. Add 6 sliced garlic cloves and a pinch of chilli flakes and cook 30 seconds. Add 600g peeled green prawns and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until just pink. Add 60ml chicken stock and the juice of 1 lemon and bubble for 30 seconds. Finish with chopped parsley. Serve straight away with crusty bread.
Crustless sandwiches of cucumber with cream cheese and dill, and egg mashed with mayo and cress, cut into neat fingers and arranged on a tiered stand.
the Hillard family home in San Francisco

Garlic-rubbed sourdough toasts topped with torn burrata, balsamic cherry tomatoes and basil, a crack of pepper and a drizzle of good olive oil. Slice 1 sourdough baguette into 16 pieces, brush with oil and grill or toast until golden, then rub with a cut garlic clove. Halve 250g cherry tomatoes and toss with 1 tbsp balsamic, olive oil and salt. Tear 2 burrata over the toasts, spoon on the tomatoes and finish with basil, pepper and a drizzle of oil.

the first dinner she has to cook for the kids
Shepherd's pie that tastes homemade because it is: lamb mince browned, onion, carrot, tomato paste and Worcestershire simmered 40 minutes, topped with buttery mash and baked at 200C until golden.
Stu's birthday dinner, the night of the cayenne pepper

Sirloin seared hard and basted with butter and thyme, sliced over crispy potatoes with a peppercorn sauce, spice kept well off the plate. Salt 4 sirloin steaks the night before. Roast 1kg diced potatoes in oil at 220C for 40 minutes. Sear the steaks in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, add 40g butter and thyme and baste for 1 minute, then rest 5 minutes. In the pan cook 1 shallot with 1 tbsp crushed peppercorns, add 150ml beef stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick.
W: when her face falls in the cake frosting
Two vanilla sponges baked at 175C, filled and covered in a thick cloud of mascarpone whipped cream, piled with strawberries. Faces stay out of it.
K: English breakfast tea brewed 4 minutes in a warmed pot, milk in first or after, sugar on the side.

Add 600g peeled green prawns and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until just pink. Add 60ml chicken stock and the juice of 1 lemon and bubble for 30 seconds. Finish with chopped parsley. Serve straight away with crusty bread.

Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, then mash with 2 tbsp mayo and chopped cress. Spread 150g cream cheese mixed with dill on bread and layer with thin cucumber. Use 12 slices white bread, cut off the crusts and cut into fingers.

m.n: The takeaway she passes off as home cooking
m.note: the first dinner she has to cook for the kids
m.how: Brown 750g lamb mince. Add 1 diced onion and 2 diced carrots, then 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and 250ml water. Simmer 40 minutes. Top with 1kg potatoes mashed with 60g butter and a splash of milk, then bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: when her face falls in the cake frosting
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Whip 250g mascarpone with 300ml cream and 2 tbsp sugar. Fill and cover the cake, then pile on 500g strawberries.

d.how: Warm the teapot with hot water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and 1L freshly boiled water, then brew 4 minutes. Pour into four cups with milk in first or after, as you like, and sugar on the side.
